note:
Reviewed opposing identities: The naval account identifies Saint Paul opposing Isabel II and Terror on 22 June. The illustration uses the armed merchant-steamer and steam torpedo-craft families; the Spanish destroyer differed in scale and gun arrangement, and Isabel II is not separately drawn. No shore-force strength or numerical loss ratio is inferred. Unavailable quantities stay empty, so these identities support an illustrative engagement rather than proportional forces.

Equipment review: the converted passenger liner Saint Paul supplies the United States auxiliary-cruiser analogy. Spain is illustrated by Terror’s steam torpedo craft family; Terror was a larger torpedo-boat destroyer, so the miniature does not reproduce its hull scale or gun arrangement. The Spanish cruiser Isabel II and coastal defences are not individually modelled.
